For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, cinematic photoreal war short based on <Picture 1>. Preserve the exact same female assassin throughout: same face, proportions, hairstyle, makeup, dress construction, body proportions, and visual texture. The entire sequence stays inside one continuous industrial brick-alley battlefield with abandoned brick walls, rusted oil drums, metal support pillars, wet concrete, and clear forward corridor depth. Lighting stays consistent: cold blue industrial ambience with warm muzzle flash, sparks, and small fire reflections. Thin smoke, dust, damp air, and gunpowder haze remain present without obscuring her face. She is cold, poised, dangerous, and extremely self-controlled, wearing a pale lavender-silver slit evening dress with metallic pearlescent sheen and high heels. Her sensuality comes only from danger, precision, breath, movement, and weapon handling, never posing. She remains in continuous motion: side-slide, wall contact, shoulder turn, pillar wrap, reload, barrel kick, diagonal advance, half-kneel stabilization, and wall-slide ending. The narrative is tactical deception: she seems pinned down, but is actually controlling the corridor while retreating and using a rolling oil drum to force the real target out from the forward depth directly in front of her. The hidden killer must never fully appear early or behind her; before the reveal, only fragmentary clues are allowed. At 00:00.000-00:01.600, open on an extreme close muzzle-flash shot. Fire, brass, and the weapon body fill the frame, then the camera slides back along the gun to her gripping hand, chest rise, collarbone, jawline, and half-side face. She fires two short bursts while side-sliding along the brick wall. Her reaction stays minimal: brows gather slightly, upper lids lower, gaze stays nailed forward, nostrils move with short breath, lips part only slightly, and the jawline remains firm. [Shot 2] At 00:01.600, move into a medium-close side-follow tracking shot as brick pillars and oil drums wipe past. She withdraws toward a brick column, taps it with her left shoulder for leverage, rotates the hips, and throws her body behind the oil drum’s side while always facing the forward corridor. Her eyes cut once toward the deep corridor as if measuring range. Brows press lower, lips flatten, side neck and shoulder tighten. Enemy rounds strike the oil drum shell, ringing the metal and throwing rust sparks. [Shot 3] At 00:03.400, deliver the dangerous close-up. A slightly low close shot rises from the hand slamming in a fresh magazine up to her lip line, nose tip, and eyes, then settles to collarbone and shoulder. Her back is against the brick pillar. She reloads cleanly, snaps the action release, and wipes soot from the edge of her lower lip with one fingertip. This beat feels dangerous, not sweet: she is reloading while waiting for prey to show itself. The outer eye lifts by the smallest fraction, then lowers; the upper eyelid loosens and tightens; one mouth corner carries the faintest bad smile; she takes one slower inhale visible in the throat and collarbone; mouth movement stays tiny and exact. She whispers, breath-close: <d>[English] Come on... show me.</d> [Shot 4] At 00:05.200, shift to a low wide-near shot emphasizing the high heels, wet reflections, dress hem, oil drum, and corridor depth. She kicks the oil drum hard, sending it rolling straight into the same forward corridor she has been watching. Instantly she turns head, shoulder, body line, gun line, and gaze into that exact forward zone. The earlier taunting vanishes at once. Brows and eyes tighten, mouth returns flat, and breathing steadies into hunter mode. Water splashes and the rolling drum echoes down the corridor. [Shot 5] At 00:06.900, the camera drops low and chases the rolling drum forward. In the foreground is the rotating barrel; in the background is the corridor end she is already targeting. Only one incomplete clue may appear at the forward cover edge: a shadow flicker, a shoe tip retracting, or a metallic corner flash. No full body reveal yet. She diagonally cuts forward by half a body width, gun held low but ready, advancing one step. Her pupils stay fixed on the corridor end, upper lids press slightly lower, jaw tucks in, lips close into a narrower line, and shoulders stay low and controlled. [Shot 6] At 00:08.600, use a slightly low medium shot from her side-front angle, keeping both her advance path and the forward cover readable. She presses one more step forward and raises the gun line at the same time. Only now is the hidden killer forced into a first full half-body reveal at the forward cover edge she has already targeted. Emphasize that the target is driven out by her control of space. She shows no surprise, only confirmation. Brows stop changing and settle flat, the gaze becomes emotionless and razor-sharp, nostril movement reduces, breathing lightens, and mouth corners remain neutral. She says coldly: <d>[English] There you are.</d> [Shot 7] At 00:10.200, keep a two-thirds body medium shot as she advances two steps and drops rapidly into a half-kneel, the camera leveling with her gun line. She raises the weapon while moving; on the second step she folds into the half-kneel and locks into a stable firing position, sight fixed on the target’s chest. Blink rate drops nearly to zero. Upper lids stay pressed, jaw tightens, lips close into a thin hard line, and breath becomes almost inaudible. [Shot 8] At 00:12.000, hold a 45-degree close medium shot that keeps her face, gun muzzle, and the target collapsing in deep background within the same frame. Do not cut to reverse. She fires one single shot only. Recoil control is clean, and the target falls backward out of the cold-lit zone. Immediately after the shot, use a brief muffled vacuum effect. Her facial response is minimal: lashes tighten slightly, the mid-face never distorts, mouth corners do not move, and there is no pleasure in the kill, only completion. Just before the shot, she says softly: <d>[English] Too late.</d> [Shot 9] At 00:13.400, finish on a slow pushing medium-close shot. Because of her earlier wound, she slides down the brick wall into a seated position, dress spread across the wet ground. Her right hand still controls the gun and keeps it pointed forward. Her left hand braces against the wet floor, fingertips pressing into the water trace. The sensuality here is not fragility but the dangerous afterglow of a threat not fully over. First a restrained exhale leaks out through nose and lips; the brow softens by a fraction; the eyes descend from full hunting focus into cold peripheral watchfulness, still aimed toward where the target fell; the lower lids show slight fatigue; finally the mouth corner lifts in the thinnest trace of satisfaction. She says low and steady: <d>[English] Now it begins.</d> Cut to black immediately after. Keep hard constraints: the audience must not see the full target before she does, the first full reveal happens only in the forward depth she has already looked at and aimed toward, and the camera must advance according to her gaze and movement direction.

overall_soundscape: Use a hollow industrial battle bed throughout: damp footsteps, rolling metal resonance, shell casings on wet concrete, bullets striking metal, action cycling, corridor echo, thin smoke movement, and restrained battlefield ambience. Emphasize near gun blast, brass, muzzle pressure, and tight breathing in the opening; shoulder impact on brick, fabric drag, oil-drum ring, and rust sparks in the side-tracking section; then close body sounds for the reload, soot wipe, slow inhale, and whispered <d>[English] Come on... show me.</d> Let the kicked drum ring hard and roll through wet echo, with only a tiny clue from the target zone before reveal. Narrow the sound field as she steps in and raises the gun, let <d>[English] There you are.</d> land dry and certain, then reduce almost everything to heels on wet ground, cloth friction, breath control, the single contained shot, brief muffled vacuum, wall-slide scrape, and the final low delivery of <d>[English] Now it begins.</d>

non_diegetic_music: Keep score minimal and tension-based, using only a low restrained pulse under the industrial ambience. Let it sit almost invisibly under the first half, increase pressure slightly during the reload taunt and barrel kick, then thin again during the reveal so spatial logic and weapon sounds dominate. After the kill shot, let the score recede into a cold low note, leaving the ending carried mainly by breath, wet room tone, and controlled aftermath.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, cinematic photoreal war-action short based on <Picture 1>, unfolding in one single continuous battlefield space centered on the abandoned armored vehicle roof and side. Keep the space physically readable at all times: hot steel, hatch, side fireline, dust, sparks, smoke, heat shimmer, metallic debris, and nearby fire reflections. Preserve the same adult female warrior: messy blonde hair, realistic sweat, dust, light abrasions, black cropped leather jacket, tactical thigh rig, tall boots, knee pads, and stable identity. Her sensuality is mature and restrained, coming only from body control, breathing, collarbone line, side face, and gaze. Use a grounded pseudo-one-take with hidden cuts, close handheld pursuit, and low gliding camera movement orbiting her relation to the vehicle surface, hatch, and side line. At 00:00.000-00:02.300, the camera glides ultra-low across the armored roof as rust, shell casings, dust, and sparks streak past. Her left palm slams onto the burning steel while her right hand carries the rifle as she cuts diagonally forward, slides on one knee, snaps the rifle up, and fires two short controlled bursts. She never freezes: she keeps pressing forward, borrowing leverage from the vehicle and shifting weight in one continuous chain. [Shot 2] At 00:02.300, the camera slides from the hand on steel past the thigh holster and engaged waist to the collarbone, neck, and half-side face. Firelight moves across her neck and jaw. Heat shimmer lifts hair strands near her lips. She never looks at the camera. Her eyes tighten first, then rise into aim. Sweat and dust hold the lashes together slightly. Brow movement stays minimal; the lower lids tighten, upper lids narrow, pupils remain stable, nostrils move with controlled breathing, and the lips stay slightly parted without widening. A short swallow passes through the throat, then neck and shoulders re-lock. At the aiming beat she says in a low tight voice: <d>[English] Come on.</d> Use a brief subtle slow-down here, then return to normal speed. [Shot 3] At 00:04.200, the camera moves into a semi-circling medium close shot. She keeps moving along the roof, completing one continuous chain of knee-slide, reach, recoil, shoulder turn, and rifle pressure while debris crosses foreground. On the third trigger pull, the rifle clicks empty with a sharp dry mechanical snap. Her reaction is microscopic: the gaze tightens for a split second, pupils pull in, the brow center deepens slightly, one mouth corner draws back, and the jaw muscle locks. Her breath shifts into one shallower quicker inhale. She immediately folds behind the half-open hatch. [Shot 4] At 00:06.600, in a tight cause-and-effect shot, she half-crouches behind the hatch. Though the rifle is empty, she keeps the muzzle high to fake suppression. Then two dull knocks sound from below. The camera follows her gaze downward. A bloodied hand reaches out from the hatch gap, and an enemy identification strip is visible on the sleeve. Her reaction is not pity or shock but rapid reassessment: her eyes drop to the hand, sweep to the marker, then return to the gap. The upper lid lifts slightly then presses down again. The brow center smooths into colder decision. Lips move from slightly open to pressed shut, lower lip drawing inward. The throat moves once, followed by the smallest downward nod. She shifts to a one-handed rifle grip and yanks the hatch with her free hand. [Shot 5] At 00:09.000, continue the pseudo-one-take into the angled vehicle side. She hooks the rifle sling through the hatch handle, turns sideways, and slides down the armored side using her body weight to wrench the hatch while kicking a nearby burning metal fragment into a leaking fuel trail. Every element stays linked in one action chain: shoulders, back, waist, legs, sling, hatch, and fireline. Her face is fully task-driven now; eyes stay on landing points, jaw locks briefly, cheek muscles tighten, and nostrils widen on short forceful breaths. The fuel catches and runs into a fast near-ground wall of flame, dangerous and close but not a giant explosion. The camera drops with her slide, and flame crosses the lens to create a hidden transition. [Shot 6] At 00:12.000, move into a vehicle-side medium close shot near half-body range. The wall of fire briefly blocks enemy sight. She bends into the hatch, drags out a wounded young soldier, and with the same motion presses his head down against her side with her forearm while moving forward along the vehicle. Give one very short lethal glance back to confirm the fire is masking them. In that glance, side face, neck line, collarbone edge, and fire-glazed jacket highlight flash together. Her breath is visible but controlled. The eyes show not softness but hard protective command. The gaze sweeps back once and returns immediately. The lip line presses flat, then opens only enough to say quietly to the soldier: <d>[English] Stay low. Move.</d> “Stay” is low and steady, “low” lands heavier, “Move” is short and direct. Her mouth closes immediately after, the corners draw inward again, and breath exits sharply through the nose. End as she pulls the boy into smoke and orange reflections, with the frame swallowed by smoke and firelight, no black screen.

overall_soundscape: The sound field is driven by close weapon fire, the dry empty-chamber click, metal scraping, boots on armored steel, controlled breathing, hatch knocks, sling tension, fuel ignition, the low ground roar of a fast fireline, and distant blurred battlefield ambience. Keep the first half tight around palm-on-metal friction, roof slide scrape, sparks, rifle bursts, breath, heat, cloth tension, and the intimate pressed-through-teeth delivery of <d>[English] Come on.</d> After the empty click, let her breathing shift immediately. Reduce broad battle noise for the hatch knocks and the scrape of the reaching hand, then build the physical chain of hatch wrenching, boot impact on burning metal, ignition hiss turning into ground fire, body slide along armor, and the strain of pulling the wounded boy free. The final beat is carried by fire, smoke, steel, movement, and her low command <d>[English] Stay low. Move.</d>

non_diegetic_music: Use almost no score. If any music is present, keep it as a very low-frequency pressure bed entering mainly in the second half. Let body noise, weapon mechanics, metal, and flame dominate. As the empty click and the bloodied hand reframe the situation, introduce a restrained low pulse; deepen it slightly when the fuel line catches and the rescue begins, but never let it overpower breath, steel, or fire. End in unresolved forward tension rather than triumph.

prompts.prompt:
A joyful young East Asian woman with long dark hair, wearing a white sleeveless top, white shorts, and white sneakers, capturing a carefree summer day.
Style
Cinematic 2000s Japanese art-house film aesthetic. Bright, airy, and nostalgic color grading with warm highlights and soft natural lighting.

Camera & Framing
Lighting consists of bright, sun-drenched summer daylight with subtle natural lens flares. Framing includes wide exterior tracking shots, high-angle crosswalk views, low-angle foot close-ups, and a medium fish-tank reflection shot.

Audio
Nostalgic acoustic indie-pop soundtrack featuring light piano melodies, gentle guitar strumming, and subtle environmental foley like flowing water and distant summer ambiance.

Realism
Photorealistic 8K rendering with natural fabric movement, realistic skin tones, accurate water reflections, and organic camera motion.

Detailed Scene Breakdown
00:00 to 00:01 features a wide back-view shot of the woman running down a sunlit sloped residential street in Japan that opens up directly to the bright blue ocean view ahead.

00:02 to 00:02 shows a medium tracking shot of her skipping happily down a quiet suburban street lined with trees and traditional walls.

00:03 to 00:04 captures a high-angle shot of her gracefully running across a white pedestrian zebra crosswalk on a sunny afternoon.

00:05 to 00:06 is a close-up shot focusing on her feet in white sneakers as she carefully walks across natural stone stepping stones over a sparkling shallow river stream.

00:07 to 00:13 features a medium shot looking through an outdoor glass goldfish tank filled with bright orange goldfish, where she walks up, leans down, and smiles warmly at the fish as sunlight reflects off the water.

prompts.prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, cinematic photorealistic image-to-video extension based on <Picture 1>. Preserve the exact same adult female character throughout: same facial structure, short hairstyle, outfit construction, body proportions, mature age impression, weapon, cargo-ship deck environment, and period texture. The whole sequence stays inside one connected ship space only: the weathered cargo deck, the container-side passage, and the visible wheelhouse zone. No harbor wide shot, no new location, no unrelated crowd. The tone is dangerous post-war allure with realism, restraint, sea wind, rust, salt mist, gulls, cold daylight, and small warm practical lights. She never poses; she stays in motion through one chain: angled sitting, rising, lifting the gun, advancing, edging along cover, stopping, aiming, confirming, lowering the gun, and looking back. Sensuality comes only from control, shoulder-neck line, breathing shifts, eye pressure, mouth tension, and her fingers on the weapon. At 00:00.000-00:02.500, she sits at an angle against the rusted ship edge. One leg extends naturally, one hand holds the rim, the other rests loosely on the gun. The camera starts low on the high-heeled ankle boots and leg line, glides past the hand on the rim, then rises to her side face and lip line. She looks only toward the sea. Her upper lids are slightly lowered, gaze stable but alive, blink rate low, breathing shallow, lips slightly parted, mouth corners neutral. Wind lifts the short front strands and hair near the ear. [Shot 2] At 00:02.500, she rises with one hand pushing off the deck while the other lifts the gun, the stock brushing the outer thigh. The camera stays close and rises with her, bringing out collarbone, shoulder line, side neck, jawline, and outer eye corner. The rise is controlled, as if fatigue remains but discipline is stronger. Her expression shifts: eyelids lift slightly, eyes move from distance to lock, the brow center gathers for a moment, lips close, the mouth line firms, and the jaw tightens lightly. A small swallow moves in the throat. In a very low soft voice, almost inside the breath, she says: <d>[English] Easy...</d> [Shot 3] At 00:04.800, a harsh cold reflection flashes from the distant container-side passage and a muted metallic hit follows. She turns immediately and advances with the gun. She does not run; she moves in a pressured fast walk with stable center of gravity, precise steps, and the gun carried low beside the thigh. The camera follows from side-rear as rusted deck textures, cables, and container edges drift behind her. Her face sharpens here: eyes lock forward, eye movement range decreases, focus intensifies, the outer eyes tighten, the brow center presses slightly, breathing shortens and quiets, lips stay closed, and the jawline hardens. [Shot 4] At 00:07.800, she skims along the container edge, stops hard, turns back through the shoulder, and raises the gun. First show the readable medium-close action, then tighten quickly into the most intimate close-up of the short. She leans into the sight line. The camera catches lashes, eye tail, side nose line, mouth corner, and the near-metal intimacy of her breath against the weapon. Her eyes do not widen; they narrow slightly, upper lid pressing down in concentration. The lower lid gathers a little, lips remain closed, one mouth corner holds a tiny natural tension, and the nostrils widen once then settle. The weapon raise is fast, sight alignment steady, and the trigger finger rests along the outside edge rather than firing. [Shot 5] At 00:10.300, as she turns past the obstruction, the gun is aimed not at an enemy but at two surviving crew members welding the deck. Welding sparks scatter, electric flicker pulses, a warm wheelhouse light turns on, and a strip of white cloth near the railing flutters in the wind. Let her subjective line of sight reveal the reversal first, then give a very short half-profile reaction. Her eyes stay guarded for half a beat, then clearly release: tension around the eyes falls slightly, upper lids lift back a little, the brow center opens, lips unseal as if a silent breath leaves, and the jawline softens from combat hardness. This is not cheerful relief, only post-threat decompression. [Shot 6] At 00:12.800, she slowly lowers the gun and lets her fingers loosen and slide along the gun body. The camera comes from behind her shoulder in a half-orbit to her side front, with warm light grazing her face. She looks back toward the sea and gives a very restrained slight smile, no teeth, only one side of the mouth lifting a little. For the first time her eyes hold softness and belonging. She says quietly: <d>[English] We’re home.</d> The line must not sound sweet or slogan-like; “We’re” is light, “home” lands lower and firmer. Her brow center is relaxed now, some fatigue remains at the eye corners, there is the slightest moisture without tears, blinking slows a little, and the mouth corner lifts then controls itself again. End mature, steady, tender, and still carrying the after-heat of war.

overall_soundscape: The soundscape is led by environment throughout: sea wind, gulls, light ship-metal creaks, heels on deck, distant electric crackle, welding sparks, low mechanical hum, and a final low ship horn. Emphasize wind, metal resonance, gulls, and her shallow breathing in the opening; hand on deck, cloth movement, gun lift, swallow, and the soft breath-close line <d>[English] Easy...</d> during the rise. Then bring in the muted metal hit, close footfalls on steel, weapon handling, cloth friction, and reduced breath as she advances. Tighten the sound field around breath and metal near the weapon during aiming, then reveal the welding reality through spark hiss, low electrical buzz, warm light switching on, white cloth in the wind, and deck machinery hum. Her final line <d>[English] We’re home.</d> should be low, close, tired, and steady, followed by wind, gulls, machinery, and the distant low horn.

non_diegetic_music: Use only a very light tension bed. Keep it minimal, cool, and modern, never epic or sentimental. Support the first half with low suspended texture, tighten slightly when the reflection and metal sound trigger her advance, thin it during the aiming close-up so breath and steel dominate, then ease the tension on the welding reveal without becoming warm or triumphant. Let the final line carry only a faint brief emotional release.

prompts.prompt:
Create a curiosity-driven character vignette built from 10–15 short cuts around the character from Image1.

Preserve the character’s identity, visual style and overall design.  Infer its nature and world directly from Image1.

Open with an immediately intriguing visual situation that creates a simple unanswered question. Build the following cuts around discovery, reaction, progression and small consequences. Each cut should introduce a new visual idea while clearly advancing the same underlying situation.

Let the character reveal itself through behavior rather than exposition. Use its movement, instincts, habits, abilities, limitations, relationships and interaction with the surrounding world to make the sequence increasingly interesting.

Keep the narrative simple enough to understand without dialogue. Create visual cause and effect between cuts. Allow details introduced early to gain meaning later. Build toward a clear reveal, reversal, transformation, emotional beat or satisfying visual payoff near the end.

Avoid generic daily routines, disconnected montage imagery and repetitive actions. Do not force familiar human behavior onto the character or world. Let the situations emerge naturally from the reference.

Make every few seconds visually distinct through changes in scale, framing, environment, movement, tension and information. Maintain strong continuity so the viewer wants to see what happens next.

Use objective third-person cinematic observation with natural handheld imperfection and varied shot sizes. Keep the camera readable, responsive and visually motivated.

Use only clean diegetic sound. No dialogue, narration, BGM, subtitles or title cards.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, cinematic photoreal dark-fantasy image-to-video sequence based on <Picture 1>. Preserve the exact same female elf warrior throughout: same face, elf ears, facial structure, hairstyle, gray-purple cloak, silver-steel armor, fitted leather battlewear, sword, body proportions, and realistic texture. The entire sequence stays inside one continuous abandoned temple interior with damp stone steps, broken archway, rough pillars, dying candles, moss, scattered leaves, wet walls, faint dust, and cold moist air. No exterior cut, no extra characters, no flashy fantasy VFX, no face drift, no identity drift. The main elf warrior advances from the lower steps toward the deeper archway. The dark counterpart always remains hidden behind a rear-side pillar and emerges physically from that same shadow, never teleporting. The tone is cold, restrained, dangerous, mysterious, and subtly sensual through presence, gaze, and motion, not posing. The main warrior’s magic exists only inside the eye: her violet eye subtly focuses inward, never emitting outward effects. The dark counterpart has the same face and species but wears a black cloak, matte dark armor, sharper shoulders, and carries cold green eyes that stay deep, stable, and clearly distinct from the warrior’s violet gaze. [Shot 2] At 00:02.200, the camera makes a low smooth push over wet steps, leaves, candle stubs, and cracked stone, then settles below and in front of the main warrior in a crouched position. One knee presses to the step, left hand braces on stone, right hand holds the sword, and the cloak falls with real weight. She is almost motionless, like a predator storing force. Her head is slightly lowered, gaze first resting on the step near her hand, lips closed, mouth corners flat, chin tucked, brow faintly gathered, and breathing nearly invisible. Only the environment moves: candle tremor, damp reflections, drifting dust. [Shot 3] At 00:04.100, cut to an intimate eye close-up. She catches that something is wrong. After half a beat of stillness, her eyes lift slowly. The violet eye does not flare; it only gathers inward with a subtle tightening deep inside the pupil. The emotional path is stillness to detection to lock. The lower eyelid tightens, breath shortens by one measure, and the lip line firms. Stay close on one eye, nose bridge, lips, and jawline as candlelight brushes her side contour. One side of her mouth lifts by the smallest amount, as if confirming a target. [Shot 4] At 00:05.400, she rises from the crouch in one swift efficient motion. The cloak swings backward with believable inertia, and the sword comes from low position into a forward guard line. She locks upright like a hunter ending concealment. Her jaw tightens, lips part only slightly to change breathing, brow compresses, and gaze hardens. Only physical feedback appears: cloak weight, slight dust disturbance, candle response. [Shot 5] At 00:06.900, she pushes quickly along the stone steps toward the deeper archway. Passing a pillar, her body skims close to the wall, the cloak brushes stone, candlelight skims her side face, and the sword stays in a ready attack-defense line. This is controlled advance, not panic. Steps stay tight, shoulders stable, head motion minimal, gaze fixed on one search line. Her eyelids narrow, breath shortens, and mouth corners flatten. At 00:08.500, she suddenly stops by half a step as if the sensed target in front has vanished. She instantly uses the pillar to half-turn, bringing the sword back toward her chest in defense. The shift is active advance to professional alert. Her eyes contract first, then broaden their search, lower lids tighten, nostrils draw slightly inward, and the lip line presses thinner. The environment feels wrong through unnatural stillness: candle motion reduces, dust slows, and the space becomes too quiet. [Shot 6] At 00:10.000, place the camera over her shoulder with part of her hood and sword edge in foreground and empty space ahead. The threat does not appear in front. Then, behind the rear pillar, the edge of a black cloak slowly slips into candlelight, followed by one black boot stepping out. The main warrior has not fully turned yet, but her back, neck, and shoulders are already tight. The dark counterpart emerges slowly on purpose, simply entering light from real shadow. The camera glides sideways and brings her fully into view: same face and species, but in black battlewear, matte black armor, sharp shoulder plates, and a long black cloak. She is darker, heavier, more severe. Her cold green eyes are deep and controlled, never neon, and one side of her mouth carries a faint wicked smile. She is not furious; she is already in control. [Shot 7] At 00:12.900, the main warrior whips around and slashes back in one immediate, accurate defensive strike. The blade cuts close past the camera line. The dark counterpart does not hurry to block. She simply steps half a step forward into the attack line and tilts her head enough for the blade to skim past. The main warrior’s intensity spikes without becoming theatrical: brow tight, nostrils slightly open, lips parted only a little from exertion, jaw rigid. The dark counterpart’s smile stays and grows colder during the head tilt, as if enjoying the failed strike. Keep the sword realistic with only restrained metallic reflection and real cloak inertia. [Shot 8] At 00:14.000, hold them in a near-distance pressure standoff. The main warrior stays lower and tighter, violet eyes sharp and loaded with both defense and attack. The dark counterpart stands more upright in black, cold green eyes fixed on her, mouth carrying a slight smile. She says in a soft, low, controlled voice: <d>[English] Now it’s my turn.</d> Do not cut to black. Instead, give a very slight forward push and stop on the two nearly identical faces with two clearly different eye colors. On “Now” the smile tightens smaller; on “my turn” the voice drops lower. After speaking, she keeps looking only at the main warrior. The main warrior does not recoil or shout; she only hardens the eyes, thins the lip line, and shows one brief throat-tightening swallow. Candle edges tremble faintly, dust remains minimal, and both violet and green eyes stay readable in the final frame.

overall_soundscape: Keep the sound field sparse, intimate, and low-frequency throughout: damp stone ambience, faint air movement, tiny candle crackle, soft cloth friction, boot contact on stone, light sword metal, and distant hollow temple resonance. Emphasize shallow breath, cloth tension, and hand-and-knee contact with wet stone in the opening; grounded cloak movement, boots, armor friction, and controlled sword handling during the rise and advance; unnatural stillness as the anomaly beat; then real physical cues for the dark counterpart’s arrival, including cloak edge, boot step, and subtle fabric drag. The slash should be sharp, restrained, and metallic, and the final line should land close, low, calm, and cold inside the attack line.

non_diegetic_music: Use minimal score or an extremely restrained dark ambient bed. Keep the first half as low suspended pressure under stillness, tighten it slightly as the main warrior rises and advances, thin it almost to nothing when the sensed target vanishes, then introduce a colder deeper tone as the dark counterpart emerges. Under the final line, let one faint low note deepen and hold without release.

prompts.prompt:
Use Reference Image 1 as the exact starting frame.

Preserve the entire screenshot faithfully, including the social media interface, profile information, embedded image, icons, buttons, layout, colors, and all elements except the post text that will physically detach from the screen.

For the first 1.5 seconds, the entire screenshot remains completely static and unchanged.

Then the visible post text begins to glow very subtly.

The post text is physically attached to the surface of the screen. The original characters themselves begin to detach from the screen one by one and rise toward the viewer as solid three-dimensional letters.

CRITICAL EFFECT:
The original 2D text must disappear from its original position at the exact moment each character detaches and rises.

Do NOT leave the original text visible underneath the floating letters.
Do NOT create duplicate text.
Do NOT keep a second copy of the post text on the screen.

Each Japanese character should behave like a physical object being lifted from the screen:
the flat character on the screen disappears as it separates,
while the corresponding three-dimensional character continues moving upward into the space in front of the screen.

From 2 to 4 seconds, the characters gradually detach from the screen and float several centimeters in front of it. Their original Japanese shapes, wording, spacing, and typography remain recognizable.

The area where the original text was displayed becomes naturally blank after the characters leave. The rest of the social media interface remains unchanged.

From 4 to 6 seconds, the detached characters hover independently in front of the screen. They have subtle three-dimensional depth, soft shadows, delicate warm illumination, and realistic spatial separation from the flat screen.

From 6 to 8 seconds, the floating characters begin moving in a smooth circular orbit around an invisible central point. The characters gradually form a graceful spiral vortex.

From 8 to 9.5 seconds, the spiral tightens and the characters are pulled toward the center of the vortex. They rotate and move deeper into three-dimensional space.

At the end, the floating characters dissolve into a small number of subtle glowing particles and disappear.

The original text does NOT return.

The final frame shows the same social media screenshot with the original post-text area now empty, while every other part of the interface remains unchanged.

Keep the camera completely static. No zoom, pan, tilt, rotation, or reframing.

Do not animate the social media interface.
Do not animate the profile picture.
Do not animate the embedded image.
Do not animate the icons or buttons.
Do not create any new text.
Do not rewrite or replace the Japanese text.
Do not duplicate the Japanese text.

The only moving elements are the original post characters after they detach from the screen, followed by their spiral motion and disappearance.

The effect should look like real physical letters being peeled away from a digital screen and released into three-dimensional space. Elegant, mysterious, cinematic, restrained, and physically convincing.

prompts.prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, dark epic war cinematic image-to-video sequence based on <Picture 1>, unfolding in one continuous snowfield frontline under a blizzard. Preserve the exact same female orc war leader throughout: same green skin, sharp face, long black hair wet with snow, heavy armor with fur collar and metal plates, and the same massive greatsword. Keep strict identity, face, armor, and weapon continuity. The distant black castle remains only background pressure and never becomes a new scene. No location switch, no giant ending wide shot, no battlefield overview, and no static posing. The tone is cold, brutal, oppressive, darkly sensual through invasive presence, wet hair, armor line, and ruthless command energy, never through posing. Wind and snow strike laterally throughout, frost clings to armor edges, breath appears as short white vapor, and the greatsword drags through snow with visible resistance, ice dust, and a sharp groove. At 00:00.000-00:03.000, the camera slides ultra-low above the snow through wind-driven grains, broken ice, and cracked crust. From the haze, the female orc leader drives into frame at speed. Her greatsword trails behind on her right, scraping the snow and cutting a long severe line. Her stride is heavy, stable, unstoppable. A few orc soldiers advance behind her in pressure formation, but she remains the focus. Her expression is hard-controlled: brow pressed down, gaze nailed forward, lips flat, jaw lightly clenched, nostrils moving subtly in the cold, breath short and heavy, with repeated white vapor from mouth and nose. [Shot 2] At 00:03.000, without cutting, the camera slides from her right-rear side into a near three-quarter side-face close shot while she keeps advancing. She sharply turns her head toward the formation behind and aside, wet hair and snow streaking across her cheek. Half her armor, neck line, collarbone edge, and sharp side profile enter frame together. Her eyes move first, then the head follows, showing precise command control. She throws one low short order: <d>[English] Move.</d> The line is cold, compressed, never shouted. A small burst of white breath leaves her lips. [Shot 3] At 00:05.000, with a violent but controlled wrist action, she flips the greatsword up from the dragging position and points it forward. Her gait shifts from heavy drive into a harder charge. The camera becomes a front-facing retreating track at medium-close distance. She is the spearhead. Behind her, soldiers ignite with her movement, raising shields and blades and roaring under pressure while snow erupts beneath repeated impacts. Her combat state hardens: gaze fully locked ahead, brow lower, eyes narrower, lips close then part briefly for a cold inhale, throat compresses, jawline tightens, and neck tendons rise. Emphasize sword-lift snow spray, real foot impact, exploding snow breakup, vibrating war gear, fur collar, leather, and armor edges. [Shot 4] At 00:08.000, still charging along the same frontline axis, the snow layer suddenly tears open beneath her path and reveals the partial body of a dead commander half-buried in snow. The camera dives with her motion over a frozen arm, broken chest plate, and packed snow, then lands on an old beast-bone clan emblem fixed to the chest armor, dusted with snow, grime, and frost. She does not fully stop. Her steps catch for half a beat, her body drops fast, and she rips the emblem from the corpse in one fierce exact movement. The emotion is subtle and brutal: eyes drop sharply, focus snaps close, brow center tightens for an instant, upper lids lift a fraction, lower lids lock, lips break from a sealed line into one tiny involuntary parting, nostrils twitch once, and the breath stops for half a beat. No tragic pause. The corpse remains only partial, frozen, and half-buried, with no horror emphasis. [Shot 5] At 00:11.000, the camera clings to her as she rises from the emblem grab, tilting upward from her hand to her face, then easing back half a step into a chest-up near shot, never widening into a battlefield climax. She clenches the old beast-bone emblem in one fist and surges upright while the blizzard hits her face head-on. Wet hair sticks across half her face. For one brief instant, pain needles across her expression: moisture flashes low in the eyes without forming tears, the inner brows pull slightly together while the outer brow stays hard, giving the feeling of hurt for one second without breaking. Her gaze drops to the emblem first, then rises forward, and at the lift of her eyes the emotion hard-cuts from pain into harsher battle intent. The upper lip lifts slightly, the lower lip tightens first and is then forced open by a roar driven from chest and throat. The mouth stays medium vertical, never too wide, never theatrical. At the same time, the greatsword sweeps across the front with her rise, her shoulder line drives forward, and she slams one step ahead as if cutting pain and rage together into the attack. The sword edge is just about to complete its strike, carrying an arc of snow powder across the near frame, when the clip cuts to black at the final instant before impact. No distant payoff, no army collision, only maximum near-character tension before release. Keep the performance micro-expressive and physical: cold pressure, command, ignition, memory stab, half-beat catch, pain flash, suppression, harder eruption. She must remain in motion throughout.

overall_soundscape: Build the scene from blizzard wind, heavy boots crushing snow, armor friction, greatsword dragging through snow, the sword being lifted and turned, and restrained roars from the orc soldiers behind her. At 00:00.000-00:03.000, emphasize lateral wind, blade drag, cracking snow crust, and her heavy cold breathing with repeated short white-vapor bursts. At 00:03.000-00:05.000, narrow the sound field around the head turn and command line; <d>[English] Move.</d> must land low, short, and hard with a small breath plume. At 00:05.000-00:08.000, intensify foot impact, shield and weapon movement, compressed war shouts, sword-lift weight, and snow erupting under repeated charges. At 00:08.000-00:11.000, sharpen inward for the dead commander reveal: rushing motion, the sudden catch in breath, the scrape of her drop, glove against frozen armor, the crack and wrench of taking the old beast-bone emblem, and a half-second interruption in breathing. At 00:11.000-00:15.000, restore full blizzard pressure against her face with hair and fur movement, armor strain, fist tightening around the emblem, the rise of the greatsword, a deeper inhale before the final roar, the compressed throat-driven roar, thicker white breath, and the snow-shearing sword pass, then cut sharply before impact.

non_diegetic_music: Use minimal dark war scoring, grounded and severe. Start with a low oppressive bass-and-drum pressure bed under the blizzard, never overpowering the physical sound design. Pull back slightly during the command line to leave room for voice and breath. As she raises the sword and the troops ignite, increase pulse and weight without becoming heroic. Thin the music for one half-beat when the emblem is revealed so the emotional stab lands through breath and tactile sound. In the final rise and roar, bring back a harder low-end surge that stops before full release, leaving the ending on suspended violence rather than completed victory.

prompts.prompt:
"Create a 15-second cinematic, photorealistic continuous-shot video based exactly on the reference image of “The Floating Night Market.”

Preserve the original architecture, floating wooden market platforms, lantern designs, vendors, customers, boats, ocean, mountains, color palette, and overall composition. Do not redesign or replace any major elements.

0–3 seconds: Begin with a slow, smooth low-angle camera movement just above the dark ocean surface, approaching the floating night market. Hundreds of warm glowing paper lanterns gently sway in the night breeze. Their golden reflections shimmer naturally across the moving water. Small waves softly move around the floating platforms.

3–7 seconds: The camera slowly rises and moves forward through the market, revealing lively activity. Vendors naturally prepare food at small wooden stalls, gently stirring steaming pots and grilling food. Thin realistic steam rises into the lantern light. Customers walk casually across narrow wooden bridges, talking and browsing. Lanterns flicker subtly and sway with the wind.

7–11 seconds: Continue the same uninterrupted camera movement with a gentle cinematic arc around the market. Small traditional boats slowly pass underneath the floating platforms. Water ripples spread behind them. Food stalls glow with warm orange and amber light while the cool blue moonlight illuminates the surrounding ocean. The huge full moon remains visible in the background behind misty mountains.

11–15 seconds: Slowly pull upward and backward into a wider cinematic reveal, showing the entire floating night market surrounded by the vast ocean. Hundreds of lanterns form a glowing trail across the water. Reflections stretch and break naturally with the waves. Mist gently drifts around the distant mountains as the moonlight creates a magical atmosphere. End on a beautiful wide establishing shot.

Visual style: ultra-photorealistic, cinematic fantasy, realistic human movement, realistic ocean and water physics, detailed wooden textures, natural lantern glow, volumetric moonlight, subtle atmospheric fog, realistic steam, shallow depth of field during close shots, cinematic 35mm photography, high dynamic range, extremely detailed, immersive scale, smooth professional camera movement.

Motion: natural human gestures, subtle wind movement, gently swaying lanterns, flowing steam, moving water, realistic boat movement, no exaggerated animation.

Camera: smooth stabilized cinematic camera, slow controlled movement, natural depth of field, gradual push-in → forward tracking → gentle arc → wide pull-back. One continuous shot with no cuts.

Negative prompt: no scene changes, no cuts, no jump cuts, no camera shake, no distorted faces, no duplicated people, no warped buildings.

prompts.prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, photoreal war-zone realism based on <Picture 1>. Preserve the exact same female protagonist throughout: same face shape, facial structure, hairstyle, costume texture, weapon design, body proportions, realistic style, and stable hand anatomy. No subtitles, no watermark, no face drift, no body distortion, no extra fingers, no weapon drift, no identity drift, and no extra characters intruding into the main action. The entire sequence stays in the same ruined urban battlefield street at dusk-to-evening, with broken high-rise remains, concrete rubble, localized fire, dense smoke, drifting embers, spent shell casings, shattered glass, and burning vehicles in the same combat space. Firelight direction and smoke flow remain consistent. The protagonist stays the visual center. The camera moves low and grounded through the same space, using close and medium-close views, with rubble, sparks, smoke, and weapon body shaping the foreground. [Shot 2] At 00:02.500, the camera pushes low through broken concrete, shells, and embers, then rises into a medium close shot on the female lead’s left-front side. She is half-kneeling with the rifle up, scanning forward, while two soldiers behind her provide brief cover from left-rear and right-rear. Her eyes are pinned forward, upper eyelids slightly lowered, breathing short and low, lips slightly parted, shoulders and neck tense, holding forced composure. The camera stays with her and makes only a small lateral move. In the background, the left-rear soldier leans out to return fire and is suddenly cut down by oblique fire from above. His body collapses believably with the impact direction. Dust and orange firelight wash across her face. Her reaction is physiological, not theatrical: jaw tightens, one shoulder contracts, eyes compress instead of widening, breath catches for half a beat, and she instantly returns to weapon control. She says in a low sharp battlefield tone: <d>[English] Get down!</d> [Shot 3] At 00:05.000, the camera sinks with her as she transitions from half-kneeling into a fully prone crawl. Stay in a tight medium-close tracking shot as she presses flat to the rubble line and slides the gun muzzle along broken concrete while searching forward. The movement feels fully physical, with real weight shift, grounded elbows, debris friction, and believable firearm mass. Her search quickens but stays controlled; nasal breathing grows heavier and mouth corners tighten. She does not scramble. Under pressure, she says: <d>[English] Night Owl One, requesting support. Repeat, requesting support.</d> [Shot 4] At 00:08.000, the camera gradually closes to a facial close shot level with her eye line. Within the same shot she searches the broken wall, the burning vehicle, and shattered glass. Then, through a passing glass reflection, a cold white identification blink appears for a split second in the upper smoke layer, revealing that the tracer origin is not the forward street line but above. The recognition beat stays restrained: she freezes for half a beat, pupils contract slightly, breathing stops once, then her eyes flick sharply upward and her lips open by only a thin line. She says in a low self-correcting tone: <d>[English] ...No. That’s wrong.</d> [Shot 5] At 00:11.000, the camera follows the motion of her weapon snapping upward and tilts smoothly into the upper smoke layer. Reveal only a brief underside silhouette of the mislocked support-fire source and its identification light, never a long full mechanical reveal. She fires two to three controlled shots upward. The target detonates in the smoke layer above, creating a sharp flash and concussive burst that lights her face from above and throws fire, dust, and fragments back into the same street space. The camera settles back onto her close shot for the ending. Her emotional state is now fully hardened: eyes shift from searching to target lock, teeth press lightly together, neck tendons rise subtly, and after firing she does not celebrate. She only stabilizes her breathing and holds a cold almost ironic aftertaste. She says in a flat controlled voice: <d>[English] Support received.</d> Keep blocking and physics coherent: the female lead remains at the front of the same rubble cover line, the two soldiers remain briefly behind her at left-rear and right-rear, her path from half-kneeling to prone crawl to upward counterfire stays physically believable, and the upper threat is revealed as a hidden layer of the same battlefield space, never a new scene. No prolonged full drone reveal, no giant air-war overview, no game HUD, no hero pose, no melodrama, no incoherent cutting.

overall_soundscape: Maintain a dense battlefield sound bed throughout: distant explosions, bullets cracking past, metal fragmentation, fire burn, dust collapse, loose debris shift, and smoke-heavy urban war ambience. Keep dialogue low, clipped, and professional. During the crawl, bring the sound close to body and gear: cloth drag, rubble scrape, breath, weapon handling, and nearby bullet snaps. For the recognition beat, briefly hollow out the wider battlefield wash and emphasize breath, ear-ringing, and directional fire streaks. The upper target detonation should hit with a heavy overhead blast, followed by falling debris and flame wash returning into the same street space.

non_diegetic_music: Use no score or only an extremely minimal low-frequency pressure bed. It must never overpower battlefield detail, breath, dialogue, or tactical realism. Thin it further during the recognition beat, then allow one restrained low-frequency surge under the upward re-aim and explosion before falling away again.

prompts.prompt:
Create a 15-second, 16:9, 24fps ultra-photorealistic live-action Y2K fashion film blended with one pure 2D manga fairy.
HIGHEST-PRIORITY RULES
Exactly TWO characters: ONE fictional 22-year-old Korean female idol + ONE tiny 2D manga fairy. No extras, duplicates, clones, motion-trail copies, or identifiable reflections.
ZERO readable text or numbers anywhere: no captions, logos, labels, signs, UI, watermarks, license plates, posters, or environmental writing.
CHARACTER LOCK
Woman: elegant oval face, cool fair skin with realistic texture, almond eyes, glossy pink lips, extremely long silky straight black hair to the waist with thin bangs. Face, hair, proportions, makeup and wardrobe remain identical.
Wardrobe: black satin cropped camisole with lace detail, cropped glossy motorcycle jacket loosely around her arms, black low-rise pleated micro skirt, silver waist chain/jewelry, black over-the-knee boots. Premium, sensual, sophisticated K-pop editorial.
Fairy: tiny PURE 2D cel-shaded manga character with clean outlines, short black hair, elf ears, large pink eyes, pink-and-white cropped top, silver pleated skirt, translucent pink wings. Always flat 2D—never 3D, photorealistic, or humanized.
ENVIRONMENT
One continuous bright pink-and-ice-blue neon fashion studio. Black vintage convertible in the center, silver vanity mirror, transparent acrylic chair, chrome spheres, silver props, glossy floor. Style: K-pop comeback film × glossy Y2K campaign × cute high-energy MV.
PHYSICAL CONTINUITY
No teleportation, clipping, spawning, or passing through objects. Fairy must physically fly above, below, around, or beside the windshield, car, mirror, chair, props, and woman. Glossy surfaces show only abstract light, never recognizable reflections.
SHOT FLOW
0:00–0:01.5 — Low-angle wide shot. Only fairy is visible behind the wheel. She waves, opens wings on beat, flies vertically until fully above the windshield, exits through the open roof, half-spins, then flies toward the woman. Driver seat becomes empty.
0:01.5–0:03.5 — Reveal woman leaning outside the car door, looking down while adjusting a ring. Fairy curves toward her shoulder and gives a TA-DA pose. The same woman raises her head, looks at fairy, then camera. Diagonal push-in from headlight.
0:03.5–0:05.5 — Woman flicks one finger toward fairy on a sharp beat. Fairy reacts with one continuous half-spin to camera-right. Woman shifts into a mischievous smile. Fast side arc; car door briefly wipes foreground.
0:05.5–0:07.5 — Fairy flies around the OUTER edge of the vanity mirror, never through it. Camera follows and finds the same woman seated on the acrylic chair. She crosses her legs and makes a tiny finger heart. Fairy hovers beside her face and imitates it. Woman smiles.
0:07.5–0:09.5 — Woman opens her palm. Fairy descends continuously and visibly lands, feet making contact. Fairy poses proudly and copies woman’s head tilt. Woman pauses, then smiles warmly. Add a cute electronic bling; push from hand toward faces.
0:09.5–0:11.5 — Fairy physically takes off from palm first. Woman stands and walks 2–3 confident steps toward center studio. Camera tracks backward with a lateral arc while fairy flies backward in front of her.
0:11.5–0:13.0 — Woman strikes a sophisticated K-pop pose with convertible diagonally behind. She touches her long hair; fairy imitates fixing her own short hair. Woman notices and breaks into a smile. Slight low-angle push-in.
0:13.0–0:14.5 — Medium close-up. Woman makes a finger heart near her face while holding her hair. Fairy hovers beside her, wings open, cheerful double-V pose. Both look into camera. Final beat triggers ONE camera flash without washing out the studio.
0:14.5–0:15.0 — Freeze the ACTUAL previous frame. No new photo, card, border, or white background. Keep neon studio, car, silver props and depth visible. Add only 4–6 small clean pink hearts/stars/sparkles near the corners, inside frame, never covering either character.
CAMERA & PERFORMANCE
Use low angles, diagonal views, subtle ultra-wide shots, foreground occlusion, mirror framing, curved push-ins, short tracking, gentle rises/drops. Avoid repetitive static frontal framing.
Emotion: cool fashion pose → curiosity → playful interaction → amused smile → joyful final pose. Natural, confident, star-like, never childish.
MUSIC
Bubblegum Pop × Kawaii Pop × Y2K Dance Pop, 125–135 BPM, punchy drums, bouncing bass, crisp claps, sparkling synths. Sync wing opening, finger flick, fairy spin, finger-heart, palm landing, takeoff, hair imitation, final pose and camera flash to major beats.
NEGATIVE

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, realistic cyberpunk tactical thriller based on <Picture 1>. Preserve the exact same female protagonist throughout: same face shape, facial features, makeup, wet hair, body proportions, black soaked tactical suit, black gloves, handgun, and weapon-mounted flashlight. Add one male tactical partner: middle-aged, short stubble, dark tactical vest, always half a step behind her as rear cover. Keep strict identity, costume, weapon, and body continuity. The entire story stays inside the same narrow neon-lit rainy alley at night, with wet pavement, red-blue reflections, damp brick walls, a garbage bin, the tail of an old parked car used later as cover, and a blurred sign deeper in the alley. The threat always comes from the deep alley direction. Do not show the shooter and do not leave this alley. [Shot 2] At 00:01.000, in a handheld medium-close tracking view just behind and right of the female lead, her gun and flashlight lead around the corner before her body. Rain streaks and wet reflections are clear. She is calm, forward-leaning, and tightly controlled, and says: <d>[English] Right side.</d> The shot shifts laterally to the male partner behind her. He raises one hand to signal stop, eyes moving first, then head, then a half-step lean to check the angle, and quietly says: <d>[English] Copy.</d> [Shot 3] At 00:03.500, the camera cuts tighter on the female lead. Her eyes scan the alley depth rapidly. Her breathing stays controlled, but her lips loosen briefly before pressing together. The warning appears through eye motion first, then eyelid tension, then a small nostril flare. Her weapon remains aligned before her body. The shot cuts to the male partner in medium close. He stops abruptly, listens into the rain and oppressive silence, and says in a compressed low voice: <d>[English] Too quiet.</d> [Shot 4] At 00:06.000, a hard cut delivers the impact beat. A suppressed shot cracks through the rain, heavy and blunt. The male partner is hit in the chest. His torso recoils backward with believable force, his strength cuts off immediately, and his gun and flashlight slip from his hand and slide across the puddled ground. No exaggerated flip and no excessive blood. The female lead snaps her head back toward him, eyes widening only slightly, mouth parting half an inch, breath catching for half a beat. [Shot 5] At 00:07.200, the camera pushes into a close shot of her face. This is the first visible break in her composure, but it lasts only a moment. Her expression cracks, then immediately refocuses on rescue. Her pupils tighten, breath sharpens, jaw sets. In a low-angle medium shot, she drops hard into the water, knees hitting the puddles, grabs his tactical strap, and drags him backward with urgent physical force. Water resistance, wet fabric drag, and body weight all read clearly. Her eyes stay locked on him as she says through the throat: <d>[English] Stay with me.</d> [Shot 6] At 00:09.800, the shot cuts to an extreme close-up of her hand and the strap. Her knuckles pale with force, the drag path scores through the thin surface water, and glove friction, strap tension, fabric strain, and water displacement feel tactile. A second unseen shot hits the ground beside her hand. Dirty water and grit burst upward. She instinctively tilts her head away and tightens one shoulder inward, then immediately keeps dragging him behind the fixed old car tail cover. The shooter remains unseen and the threat direction stays the same. [Shot 7] At 00:12.500, from behind cover in a close shot, she presses her earpiece and calls for backup while keeping her eyes pinned toward her wounded partner in the rain. Her breathing is fast, throat working visibly, shoulders tense, posture still pitched forward as if she wants to go back out. She says: <d>[English] A-17 requesting backup. Officer down.</d> Then, in the same setup with a slight push-in, she repeats in a lower more urgent tone: <d>[English] Repeat, officer down.</d> [Shot 8] At 00:13.800, the command voice comes through the earpiece: <d>[English] Abandon the wounded. Retreat now.</d> The line cuts through her like a blade. Her urgency freezes mid-expression. She looks down once at the hand gripping the strap, then slowly releases it. After that she raises the gun again and re-aims toward the alley mouth. The emotional transformation is visible in order: the eyes stop first, then the breath flattens, then the mouth and jaw harden, then the body returns to tactical alignment. End on this steady forced return to duty in the same alley space and the same threat direction. Keep the performance micro-expression driven and restrained: calm command, tightening alertness, sudden breach, instinctive rescue, forced emotional severance, restored execution mode. No screaming, no crying collapse, no overacted emotion, no visible shooter, no cutaway, no extra people, no subtitles, no watermark.

overall_soundscape: Continuous layered rain runs through the full 15 seconds with wet pavement hiss, neon hum, damp alley ambience, subtle gear rustle, and restrained weapon handling. The suppressed shot should sound heavy and blunt, followed by body impact, dropped weapon, flashlight clatter, water drag, strap strain, sharp breathing, earpiece static, and the cold detached command voice. Keep all dialogue dry, low, intimate, and tightly synced to small mouth movement.

non_diegetic_music: Use little or no score. If any score is present, keep it extremely minimal as a faint low-frequency pressure bed, never overtaking rain, breath, dialogue, or tactical detail. Let the ending feel nearly bare, carried mainly by rain, breath, and the return of aim.

prompts.prompt:
text rule: every section label and descriptive sentence is silent production direction, never speech content. Do not speak, recite, chant, sing, or read this prompt aloud.
Background music: enabled. Generate a context-appropriate non-diegetic score unless the user explicitly requests silence or no music.
Dialogue permission is enabled, but this plan contains no dialogue lines. Generate no character speech, conversation, chanting, singing, or other vocals.
Dialogue language: automatic. Preserve each explicit <d> language tag; otherwise use the language required by the scene and user intent.
Narration: disabled. Generate no narrator, voice-over, spoken description, or audible reading of prompt text, section labels, instructions, asset tags, or metadata.
Subtitles: disabled. Do not render subtitles or dialogue captions.
Creative direction (authoritative within explicit user intent and reference fidelity)
Priority: Apply these creative directives clearly wherever they do not conflict with explicit user requirements, identity retention, or fixed first/last-frame composition.
Format and direction: Favor believable observation, motivated reframing, natural performance, and environmental detail over polished spectacle. Retain small imperfections that support authenticity while keeping the subject readable. Progress from a human-scale anchor to environmental scale, preserving depth layers and landing on a strong reveal composition.
Camera execution: Follow the action continuously in a single unbroken take, using only motivated pans, small translations, and reframing needed to preserve spatial clarity.
Look: Treat connected visual references as authoritative for identity, wardrobe, objects, environment, composition, lighting, color, and medium; do not impose an unrelated restyle.
Pacing and composition: Use moderate, readable motion with natural acceleration and enough settling time for each important beat. Use exactly one continuous shot with no hidden or explicit cuts; express all action beats through blocking, performance, camera motion, reframing, and synchronized sound. An explicit user-requested shot or cut count remains authoritative over this density preference. Compose for a vertical frame: protect faces, hands, and essential action inside the central mobile-safe area; favor depth movement and avoid losing subjects at narrow side edges.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> -> identity: Use the supplied collage as the authoritative visual reference for the same woman’s identity, facial features, pale skin, long dark hair in an elaborate updo with pale ornaments, downcast gaze, refined feminine silhouette, pale silver-gray embroidered gown, fitted bodice, flowing floor-length skirt, gold floral ornamentation, jeweled details, translucent wide-sleeved shawl, garment rack, bright ornate interior, tall windows, pale-blue mountain scenery, decorative furnishings, warm small lights, oval mirror, layered depth, luminous window backlight, cool silver-blue and warm champagne palette, detailed textiles, graceful portrait and near-full-body framing, and polished dreamlike fashion-editorial treatment. Preserve these elements consistently throughout one continuous scene, while treating the collage as a reference rather than reproducing its nine-panel layout. Use the depicted poses to guide the natural action of lifting the sheer garment, draping it around the shoulders, checking the waist and silhouette, and turning toward the mirror with quiet delight. Present the performance with believable observational imperfections and tasteful focus on clothing, posture, silhouette, and fabric movement..

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] At 00:00.000-00:15.083, At the start, <Subject 1> stands beside the pale garment rack in the luminous ornate interior, already wearing the pale silver-gray embroidered gown and holding the translucent shawl. She notices the garment with quiet anticipation, lifts it carefully, and brings it around her shoulders. Her expression changes into visible, restrained delight as the sheer fabric catches the window light. Without any cut, she smooths the shawl and checks the embroidered waist and flowing skirt, allowing the camera to follow her natural movement and preserve her graceful silhouette. She takes a few small steps toward the oval mirror, turns slightly to inspect the front and rear drape, then settles into a poised full-body stance with a soft satisfied smile and a brief downward glance at the finished outfit. The performance is tasteful, realistic, and focused on the pleasure of trying the new clothing. Camera: Start in a stable medium three-quarter view beside the garment rack, with the woman centered in the mobile-safe area. Slowly track laterally and forward with her as she lifts the translucent shawl, maintaining natural handheld steadiness and mild human-scale imperfection. Arc subtly around her front as she drapes it and checks the waist, preserving face and hands. Continue with a small motivated translation toward the oval mirror, then ease backward and slightly lower to reveal the full gown, shawl, elegant posture, bright windows, and layered interior depth. Land on a composed near-full-body reveal with the woman centered and the mirror and mountain-lit windows supporting the background. Motion: Moderate readable movement only: lift the shawl, drape it, smooth the shoulders and waist, make a small turn, walk a few measured steps, and settle. The camera accelerates gently with her initial movement, follows with restrained parallax around her, and decelerates before the final reveal. Fabric responds naturally to each hand movement and settles before the ending pose. Synchronized audio: 0.8-2.2s: soft hanger and translucent-fabric rustle as she lifts the shawl; 3.0-6.0s: continuous fabric movement while she drapes the shawl over both shoulders; 7.0-9.5s: delicate dress and shawl rustle as she adjusts the waist and turns; 10.0-12.0s: quiet measured footsteps toward the mirror; 12.5-15.083s: fabric settles as she holds the final pose; music reaches a gentle resolution

overall_soundscape:
Natural quiet interior ambience under the music: light fabric rustle as the shawl moves, restrained footsteps, a faint clothing-rack or hanger sound, and subtle room resonance. No narration or spoken voice. No narration, voice-over, spoken description, or audible prompt reading.

non_diegetic_music:
Soft elegant instrumental music with delicate strings, airy piano, and subtle shimmering tones; begin quietly, gently lift during the shawl reveal, and resolve softly at the final pose. No lyrics or vocal music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, realistic night-market drama based on <Picture 1>. Preserve the exact same young female barbecue vendor throughout: same face, skin texture, hairstyle, clothing cut, age impression, body proportions, and stable anatomy. She remains a real stall owner, not a posing model. No subtitles, no watermark, no extra core characters, no scene jump, no prop drift, no face deformation, and no exaggerated mouth movement. The entire short stays inside the same open-air night market barbecue stall space: grill front, stall side, prep counter edge, and the small two-step area in front of the camera. Red charcoal glows, white smoke drifts, grilled meat shines with fat highlights, and warm string lights and stall lamps create soft background bokeh. Condiment bottles, plates, skewers, tongs, and prep bowls stay consistent. Background market activity remains blurred and natural. The story is about relational control: she notices the unseen watcher behind the camera, uses grilling to lure that person closer, seems ready to offer a skewer, then suddenly takes it back and reclaims control. The camera feels like a subjective viewpoint being led by her, moving in one smooth line: low close glide, gentle push to eye contact, half-orbit with her body, small retreat under her pressure, then a clean turn back to the grill. [Shot 2] At 00:02.200, the camera rises from glowing charcoal and meat to her hands and lower face as she turns skewers with practiced wrist control. Her breathing is calm, lips relaxed, and she does not look at the camera yet. Then she lifts her eyes and fully locks onto the camera for the first time. After a half-second hold, one corner of her mouth lifts slightly. She keeps turning skewers and says with light provocation, <d>[English] You’ve been watching for a while...</d> [Shot 3] At 00:04.500, she selects the best-looking skewer with metal tongs and shifts half a step away from the grill. Firelight brushes her side face and collarbone. Her shoulders and neck open naturally without posing. Her smile softens into something more ambiguous as if she is deciding for the watcher. She says, <d>[English] So, are you gonna try one?</d> [Shot 4] At 00:06.800, the camera enters an intimate close-up. She brings the skewer near her lips to test the heat, exhales softly across it, and never breaks eye contact. Her eyelids lower slightly, then lift again. Her lips part only minimally. She does not lick her lips and does not bite the meat. The mood is controlled, soft, and deliberate. [Shot 5] At 00:08.900, she walks two slow steady steps toward the camera from the grill side toward the stall edge near the prep counter. The camera yields backward slightly but stays in the same stall space. Her center of gravity leans subtly forward. The smile reduces and her eyes tighten. The atmosphere shifts from flirtation into mild pressure as she says in a closer lower tone, <d>[English] Keep staring, and it’ll get cold.</d> [Shot 6] At 00:11.700, she extends the skewer toward the camera until the tip lightly touches the lens edge, creating the feeling that she is about to hand it over. At the exact moment of apparent giving, she suddenly pulls it back. She leans in closer, narrows her eyes slightly, and half the smile disappears. Her tone drops into quiet command as she says, <d>[English] If you want it, come get it yourself.</d> She does not wait for a response. Immediately after the line, she turns back cleanly to the grill, presses the same skewer over the heat, and a fresh flare of fire rises. End on the return to the charcoal and her reclaimed control. Keep the performance restrained and realistic: relaxed discovery, playful testing, soft seduction, close pressure, then withdrawal and counter-control. Build everything through eyes, mouth corners, breath, jaw, shoulders, neck, and fingers, never through broad expression or crude seduction. Maintain stable stall geography, realistic smoke and fire physics, natural hand anatomy, believable eye motion, continuous hair and costume behavior, and premium cinematic texture.

overall_soundscape: Realistic night-market ambience runs throughout with charcoal crackle, fat sizzling, light tong contact, blurred distant voices, utensil sounds, and warm outdoor stall hum. Keep her dialogue intimate, low, and natural. Add a soft cooling breath near the skewer, small footstep sounds as she approaches, a tiny metallic contact when the skewer tip touches the lens edge, then a strong renewed sizzle and brief fire flare when the skewer returns to the grill.

non_diegetic_music: Use little or no score. If present, keep it minimal and low, more like a subtle tension bed than a melody. Let the final power shift be carried mainly by her voice, breath, grill sizzle, and the closing flare.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, realistic cyberpunk thriller. The first frame fully matches <Picture 1>. Preserve exact continuity throughout: Subject A is the driver with black hair, a cold restrained expression, a mechanical prosthetic arm, and the same white heavy motorcycle; Subject B is the rear passenger with red hair, a pale trench coat, wet hair clinging to the skin, and an initially fragile but later dangerous presence. Keep the same faces, hair colors, body proportions, age impression, costumes, prosthetic details, and motorcycle design from <Picture 1>. No new characters, no costume or hairstyle drift, no face drift, no body drift, no subtitles, no watermark. The entire story stays inside the same narrow rain-soaked cyberpunk alley near the reflective wet wall at the alley end. The ground is slick, the walls are damp, neon signs cast mixed red and blue reflections, the air holds cold mist, and the space feels compressed. The camera is intimate and functional, using a few dense close and medium-close shots; the first half flows, the second half steadies. A always remains in front controlling the motorcycle with a low forward lean. B always remains pressed close behind, first dependent, then silently dangerous. [Shot 2] At 00:02.500, the camera cuts from an ultra-low tracking view near the front wheel tearing through rainwater, rises into A’s half-profile, then drifts to the rear-view mirror where B’s eyes appear. B breathes slightly fast, glances toward the pressure behind them, then toward A, and quietly says: <d>[English] They’re close.</d> A stays controlled and forward-facing. [Shot 3] At 00:05.500, the shot cuts to a diagonal rear medium-close tracking angle as the motorcycle leans low and skims past the wet wall. Red and blue neon sweep across both faces. B presses closer and grips A’s waist side, implying dependence. A does not turn back, only checks B once through the rear-view mirror, then says in a low compressed tone: <d>[English] Hold on. Don’t look around.</d> The line feels protective and commanding. [Shot 4] At 00:08.500, the shot cuts tighter on both upper bodies, then pushes into an extreme close-up of B’s hand. Still pressed close, B silently draws a thin blade or micro-injector from inside the trench coat and brings it to the side of A’s neck. The move is small, efficient, and nearly hidden by their intimacy. B’s eyes lock cold, her mouth line flattens, her breathing stabilizes, and the false helplessness disappears. She says quietly and precisely: <d>[English] You didn’t come to save me.</d> [Shot 5] At 00:11.500, the camera alternates between an extreme close-up of A’s eye and the rear-view mirror. A remains unnervingly steady, then gives a short controlled brake tap. The motorcycle decelerates just enough on the wet road to throw B’s body forward by half an inch and spoil the weapon angle. At the same instant, A’s left shoulder drives subtly backward to steal space. The action stays fully physical and believable through brake pressure, slick-road resistance, inertia, and the tiny forward jolt. A calmly replies: <d>[English] And you didn’t come to leave with me.</d> [Shot 6] At 00:13.000, the motorcycle performs a precise sliding stop at the alley end in front of the reflective wet wall. The camera moves to a front-side 45-degree angle and settles into a composition where both characters appear together in the reflective wall surface. The geometry locks them in the same frame. A’s hidden countermeasure device is already raised in the other hand, aimed at B through the reflected composition. A lifts the gaze toward B’s reflection rather than turning into a dramatic pose and says in a low voice: <d>[English] The moment you got on, I was waiting for this.</d> B does not explode emotionally; she only shows a brief stall and tightened pupils. Hold on the reflected standoff through the end, with no fade to black and no cut away. Keep the acting restrained and realistic: A stays cold, minimal, and highly controlling, with eyes moving before speech and very little mouth or jaw change; B begins with quick breath, wet-hair vulnerability, and help-seeking closeness, then becomes cold and controlled after the weapon reveal. Lighting stays cold and wet with red-blue neon sweeps, motorcycle headlight shaping the bodies, realistic wet skin, subtle prosthetic highlights, visible road oil and damp wall texture, and preserved detail in the dark areas. Maintain spatial and physical coherence in the same alley from start to finish with no teleporting, no wide fight, no extra vehicles intruding, no exaggerated stunts, no cartoon expression, no face collapse, no oversized mouth shapes, no limb deformation, and no overacting.

overall_soundscape: Heavy realistic rain runs through the full 15 seconds with tire spray, wet-road hiss, subtle electric motor presence, close urban electrical buzz, and damp-wall reflections. Dialogue stays tightly synced to restrained mouth movement and breath rhythm. Add wet fabric friction, the faint blade or injector reveal, a short brake tap, slick-pavement tire friction, the tiny forward body jolt, the controlled sliding stop, scattered water, and a subtle readiness sound from A’s hidden countermeasure.

non_diegetic_music: A low-frequency suspended electronic thriller score with minimal melody. Keep it understated under the rain and vehicle motion, tighten it after B’s weapon reveal with colder pulses, add a brief tension accent at the brake-tap reversal, and thin it slightly in the final reflective standoff while preserving unresolved pressure.
